title: Projectivity and geometric fibres of an arithmetic nodal point blowup
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X$ be Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian) [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $f:X\to S$ be H-projective, meaning it factors as a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over $S$ [def-kun-projective]. Let $x\in X$ be a closed point of the special fibre. Suppose there are a local injective etale extension of DVRs $R\to R'$ for which $\pi$ remains a uniformizer, an integer $n\geq2$, and etale $S$-maps $(X,x)\leftarrow(U,u)\to(M_n,o)$, where $M_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R'[a,b]/(ab-\pi^n))$ and $o=(\pi,a,b)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Put $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_xX\to X$, the ordinary blowup of the reduced point [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Assume $g=f\circ b$ is flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then both $b$ and $g$ are H-projective and proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]; $g$ is flat and finitely presented, and $B$ is Noetherian. Every fibre $b^{-1}(y)$, $y\in X$, is nonempty and geometrically connected over $\kappa(y)$, that is, connected after base change to every field extension of $\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; in particular every geometric fibre of $b$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. More precisely, away from $x$ the fibres stay single points after arbitrary residue-field extensions; over an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ the exceptional fibre is isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ if $n=2$, and to two copies of $\mathbf P^1$ meeting at one reduced point if $n>2$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-sc-p1-standard, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Consequently $b$ is surjective, and nonemptiness of every geometric fibre of $f$ implies nonemptiness of every geometric fibre of $g$. No connectedness of the fibres of $f$ or $g$, split-node hypothesis over $\kappa(x)$, excellence or characteristic restriction is imposed.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I$ be the ideal of the reduced closed point $x$. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] it is quasi-coherent and on each affine open it is an ordinary ideal. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, each of these ideals is finitely generated, so $\mathcal I$ is of finite type. The DVR $R$ is Noetherian by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-affine-base-blowup] to $A=R$, the given H-projective $f$, and $\mathcal I$. Both $b$ and $g$ are H-projective. Apply [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] to each to obtain properness.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); H-projectivity supplied by the existing affine-base theorem

proof.text: Properness includes finite type and separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $g$ is quasi-compact and, by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], quasi-separated. Together with the assumed local finite presentation, the definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] gives finite presentation. Flatness is already assumed. Since $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is Noetherian and $g$ is finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $B$ is Noetherian.

Put $l=\kappa(x)$, $k_o=\kappa(o)=R\prime/(\pi)$ and $L=\kappa(u)$. The two etale maps have discrete reduced fibres consisting of spectra of finite separable residue extensions by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points]. Write $p:U\to X$ and $q:U\to M_n$. Since $x$ and $o$ are closed points, the fibres $p^{-1}(x)$ and $q^{-1}(o)$ are closed in $U$. Each is discrete, so $\{u\}$ is open in it and $p^{-1}(x)\setminus\{u\}$, $q^{-1}(o)\setminus\{u\}$ are closed in the fibre, hence closed in $U$. Remove these two closed sets from $U$; the restrictions of $p$ and $q$ to this open neighbourhood of $u$ remain etale. On the resulting common neighbourhood, both scheme-theoretic inverse images are exactly $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Etaleness gives flatness by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] with its comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] to both maps. Taking their fibres at $u$ gives $E_x\times_l L\cong E_o\times_{k_o}L$, where $E_x=b^{-1}(x)$ and $E_o$ is the exceptional fibre of the model point blowup. This uses the whole fibre via the Cartesian squares, not just an etale cover of it.

source.place: Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), shrinking U and the two Cartesian squares

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-binomial-blowup-chart-algebras] with domain $R\prime$, nonzero element $\pi$ and exponent $n$. Its extended-ideal quotients and overlap maps give a cover of $E_o$ by $\operatorname{Spec}k_o[t]$, $\operatorname{Spec}k_o[r,s]/(rs-\epsilon)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k_o[h]$, with $\epsilon=1$ for $n=2$ and $0$ for $n>2$. For $n=2$ the middle open is the common punctured affine line and $h=t^{-1}$. These are precisely the two standard charts of $\mathbf P^1_{k_o}$ in [def-sc-p1-standard]. For $n>2$ the closed subschemes $s=0$ and $r=0$ of the middle chart extend respectively across the first and third outer charts. The overlap coordinates are $r=t^{-1}$ and $s=h^{-1}$; each closed subscheme is therefore $\mathbf P^1_{k_o}$. They cover $E_o$ scheme-theoretically since $(r)\cap(s)=0$ in $k_o[r,s]/(rs)$, and their scheme-theoretic intersection is $\operatorname{Spec}k_o$ since the sum of the ideals is $(r,s)$. This proves the stated configuration including reducedness of the intersection. All the displayed quotient rings and substitutions stay the same after every field extension of $k_o$.

source.place: Tag 0CDC (example-blowup); elementary gluing from the existing chart-algebra statement

proof.text: Over every field $F$ extending $k_o$, each standard affine line of $\mathbf P^1_F$ is irreducible: the zero prime of $F[t]$ belongs to every nonempty basic open. The two affine lines meet in $\operatorname{Spec}F[t,t^{-1}]$, so their union is nonempty and connected. In the two-component case a clopen partition restricts to a trivial partition on each of the two projective lines; their common $F$-point forces both lines into the same part. Thus $E_o$ is nonempty and geometrically connected. Step 3 and [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-check-after-extension] first give geometric connectedness of $(E_x)_L$ and then of $E_x$ over $l$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed], embed the finite separable extension $L/l$ into an algebraic closure $\bar l$. Base changing the isomorphism of Step 3 to $\bar l$ and using Step 4 identifies $(E_x)_{\bar l}$ with exactly the asserted projective-line configuration. This does not assert that its components are individually defined over $l$.

Step 2: proper ⇒ finite type, separated ⇒ quasi-separated, so g is finitely presented and B is Noetherian. Step 3: the étale fibres are reduced, discrete and separable; after shrinking, both extended ideals are the reduced point u, and the Nagata flat-base-change comparison gives E_x×_l L ≅ E_o×_{k_o} L over L. Step 4: I checked the gluing myself. For n=2 the middle chart lies in chart 1 and the result is P¹. For n>2 the two lines are {s=0} with chart 1 and {r=0} with chart 3, chart 1 ∩ chart 3 is empty, (r)∩(s)=0 in k[r,s]/(rs), and (r)+(s)=(r,s), so they meet in a reduced point. Step 5: geometric connectedness passes from k_o to L to l via 054N, and embedding L/l into l̄ gives the configuration. Step 6: b is an isomorphism off x, so it is surjective; surjectivity survives base change, so nonempty geometric fibres of f give nonempty ones of g. Edge cases checked: n=2 in characteristic 2, n=3, n≥4, imperfect or inseparable residue fields, empty generic fibre.
